data.title: There May Be Underlying Issues With The Quality Of GAON CABLE's (KRX:000500) Earnings
data.description:
GAON CABLE Co., Ltd. (KRX:000500) announced strong profits, but the stock was stagnant. Our analysis suggests that this might be because shareholders have noticed some concerning underlying factors.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Examining Cashflow Against GAON CABLE's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. To quote a 2014 paper by Lewellen and Resutek, "firms with higher accruals tend to be less profitable in the future".

GAON CABLE has an accrual ratio of 0.32 for the year to September 2026. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, raising questions about how useful that profit figure really is. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₩194b despite its profit of ₩75.6b, mentioned above. We saw that FCF was ₩48b a year ago though, so GAON CABLE has at least been able to generate positive FCF in the past.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

• Nokia is part of the newly formed AI Gigafactory Northern consortium, which aims to deploy distributed, low-carbon AI infrastructure across Nordic and Baltic data centre sites and has also agreed to supply autonomous network solutions to One New Zealand to support higher levels of AI-driven network operations.
  • The twin focus on EU-governed AI infrastructure and AI-native telecom networks gives Nokia a clearer role in trusted, sovereign-grade digital plumbing, which directly links its connectivity products to future AI and cloud demand rather than only traditional mobile network cycles.
  • We will now examine how Nokia's investment narrative, built around AI and cloud-driven growth, could shift with its AI Gigafactory role.

Nokia Oyj Investment Narrative Recap

Nokia Oyj attracts shareholders who see value in its role as a supplier of core network, cloud and AI infrastructure, with earnings forecast to grow 33.07% a year and revenue expected to rise 6.4% a year faster than the Finnish market. According to TheTurntTomato, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, that growth story is supported by a solid cash position and expanding AI exposure.

Right now, the key near term swing factor is execution on AI and cloud driven contracts while managing a P/E of 50.6x versus a European communications average of 16.1x. The biggest operational risk remains volatile earnings quality, including large one off items and a relatively low 3.7% return on equity. The new AI initiatives do not immediately change this.

The AI Gigafactory Northern consortium looks most relevant for Nokia Oyj because it links directly to AI infrastructure demand in Europe and leans on Nokia’s strength in secure connectivity. This project aligns closely with the existing thesis that AI and cloud workloads can support earnings that analysts expect to grow significantly over the next three years.

Execution is the real test. Nokia needs to win tenders, deliver the networking layer across multiple Nordic and Baltic sites and convert this role into recurring revenue, all while handling a share price that has been highly volatile over the past three months. If AIGF Northern moves from concept to contracted capacity, it could become an important proof point for that AI led growth narrative described by TheTurntTomato.

TheTurntTomato argues that Nokia can justify a fair value of €15.16 if it compounds revenue at 23.8% a year and eventually settles at a 3.9% profit margin. Together, these assumptions would support higher earnings power from its AI, telecom and defense exposure.

Exploring Other Perspectives

One catalyst the bearish Nokia analysts keep circling is execution risk on the massive restructuring program. You can see it in their numbers. They were only pencilling in 4.6% annual revenue growth and earnings of €2.4b by 2029, which is far more cautious. Those views all came before this AI Gigafactory news, so some opinions may evolve.
